note: FDIC balance sheet, 30 June 1956. Scanned with an OCR layer. Every subtotal exact and the sheet balances: assets = liabilities + fund = 1,822,462,212.
FDIC statement of income and deposit insurance fund, FY1956. Its closing fund figure 1,690,818,394 also appears on fdic_balance -- a cross-page invariant.

Table 114, earnings and expenses of insured commercial banks by state. Landscape on a portrait page, 33 rows and 11 numeric columns. TWO-DIMENSIONAL ARITHMETIC, and the two directions are not equally strong: ACROSS each row the US column equals Alaska plus Puerto Rico plus Other plus Continental US, exact to the unit on all 33 rows; DOWN each column the components miss the printed total by 1 to 4, because amounts are printed in thousands and each is rounded on its own, so those sums carry tolerance 5. Six of the eleven columns are labeled: the five that carry the row identity, plus Connecticut, the rightmost column on the page.

1929 Census of Manufactures schedule, sheet 2, FILLED IN BY HAND. Employees, salaries, materials and products. Three handwritten sums check: 10,951 + 60 + 300 = 11,311; 3,120 + 6,630 + 14,500 = 24,250; 1 + 2 = 3 salaried men. Struck-through corrections, marginal annotations in other hands, noisy skewed grayscale scan.

Same schedule, sheet 3. Sparse hand-filled form: power equipment, fuel, distribution of sales. 35,000 + 2,000 = 37,000 checks against the handwritten total. Two signatures, and 'x x x x x' fill patterns in cells that do not apply.

FDIC Annual Report 2023, Deposit Insurance Fund balance sheet as of December 31, printed page 132. THE ONLY BORN-DIGITAL PAGE IN THE CORPUS: typeset by InDesign, with a real text layer rather than somebody else's OCR over a photograph of paper. It is the SAME PUBLICATION as fdic_balance, 67 years later, which makes the pair a direct measurement of what the text layer is worth -- the 1956 sheet is a scan carrying an ABBYY layer, this one was never scanned at all. TWO YEAR COLUMNS (2023 and 2022), so a parser must keep them apart; NEGATIVE FIGURES IN PARENTHESES; and four figures embedded in label prose, two per year. Ten sums, all exact to the dollar, and the sheet balances in both years.
